0.0.n: さん makes this a polite, friendly way to address the audience.

0.1.n: A standard daytime greeting; its final は is pronounced わ.

0.3.n: This is the speaker’s name, written in katakana.

0.4.n: A polite sentence ending used after a name to introduce yourself; I is left unstated.

1.0.n: Read きょう here; it names the day being discussed.

1.1.n: Marks today as the topic of the sentence.

1.2.n: Names the day of the week; the sentence continues without an explicit is after it.

1.4.n: A shortened form of コンビニエンスストア, describing where the new products are sold.

1.5.n: 新 means new, and 商品 means products; together they describe what is being released.

1.6.n: 発売 means going on sale, and 日 adds day; here 日 is read び.

1.7.n: Marks release day as the status described by なっております.

1.8.n: なる becomes なって plus おります, a humble, formal version of います; here it politely states the schedule.

2.0.n: Sets the time frame for checking the products.

2.1.n: Replaces は after 今週, suggesting the speaker does this in other weeks as well.

2.2.n: Can cover various bakery items, not just loaves.

2.3.n: Joins パン and スイーツ into a pair of product categories.

2.4.n: A borrowed word commonly used for desserts and sweet treats.

2.5.n: Marks bread and sweets as the starting point for the product review.

2.6.n: チェックする becomes チェックして plus いきましょう, politely inviting viewers to begin and continue checking together.

3.0.n: 買う becomes 買って plus きた, showing a purchase followed by returning; the phrase directly describes 商品.

3.1.n: The preceding 買ってきた specifies which items the speaker means.

3.2.n: Marks the products the speaker bought as the topic.

3.3.n: Politely points to the items being shown; です is left unstated.

0.tip: Japanese often leaves out I when introducing yourself with a name plus です.

1.lit: Today, as for, Tuesday; convenience store new products’ release day it is.
1.tip: となっております is a formal way to state the schedule here, rather than describe an actual change.

2.lit: This week too, starting with bread and sweets, let’s go on checking!
2.tip: から shows which categories the speaker will check first.

3.lit: Bought and brought back products, as for, these here!
3.tip: 買ってきた comes before 商品 to describe the products, without needing a word like that.
